Author: Claude
Message:
explorer: the block surface and a search box that admits what it cannot know

Blocks by slot, block detail, the recent-blocks stream, and the search that
reaches them. Read from the archivals (139.180.166.5 / .173.231) through a new
`/g4` Pages Function, never from a validator: the node RPC has no auth, no rate
limiting, and shares a thread with consensus.

Three things drove the design, all measured against the live chain.

**A slot has three states, not two.** 38.2% of slots carry no block (20,895 of
54,719 at the time of writing), including a ~15,000-slot stretch around slots
18,500-33,500 where the chain barely produced. But the archivals also drop
about one read in twenty, and a timeout is not a missed proposal. Rendering the
second as the first invents a miss and attributes it to a validator who
proposed. `SlotCell` makes them separate variants and the table draws them
differently; `SlotTally` counts them apart.

**Finality is a reading, not a property.** The finalized checkpoint is not a
latch across a reorg — `do_reorg` adopts an ancestor's state with no comparison
of incoming against outgoing — so a block returned `finalized: true` can come
back `justified`. No badge says settled, confirmed or irreversible. The block
page instead shows what the reading clears: the node's word, whether two
archivals concur on root and epoch, and whether it is +3 epochs past finality,
with the note that no depth is provably safe while the quorum denominator has
no floor. This also removes `recentBlocks`' cache, which kept any block with
`finalized: true` forever and would have gone on serving reorganised blocks.

**There are no transaction ids, and that is the search box's hardest case.**
`gettransaction` is refused permanently (-32005) and `sendrawtransaction`
returns a node-local hash others do not agree on. Feeding one to `gettxout`
returns a clean `unspent: false` — verified live with 32 bytes of `ab`, HTTP
200, no error — indistinguishable from a spent output or a dropped withdrawal.
So a 32-byte value that is neither a block nor a funded script hash routes to
/tx, which demonstrates that trap on the reader's own input and sends them to
the lookups that are exact.

Also: a bare number is no longer silently read as a slot. Slot and height are
20,895 apart and there is no `getblockbyheight`, so the box offers both and
resolves a height by closing a bracket on it (height is monotone in slot);
measured 16 probes for dense heights, and it reports the bracket rather than
guessing when the stall defeats it. `agree()` verifies via `x-bloch-node-index`
that two answers came from two different boxes, so a single-upstream transport
degrades to "no cross-check was possible" instead of a false agreement.

Verified by rendering the real components against the live chain: 45 checks
covering all three slot states, the four block-page answers, the search
grammar, the tx trap and height search; plus 9 against the Function itself
(allowlist, per-node pinning, failover, and not failing over on -32007).

Author: Claude
Message:
docs(integration): recover the two unlanded Genesis-4 documents, with every claim re-checked

BLOCH-G4-TRANSACTIONS.md (1,257 lines) and BLOCH-G4-RPC.md (1,213 lines) were
written on 2026-08-13 "from measurement" and never landed. Each existed on one
machine-named branch and on no other ref; both branches are on a deletion
list. The measurement in them is worth keeping — the cryptographic core of the
transaction document was independently reproduced here, digit for digit.

They are NOT landed on trust. This tree's failure mode this week has been a
statement that was true when written and false two weeks later, and a document
that says "measured" carries that at full strength because it reads as
evidence. Every falsifiable claim was re-checked against this commit's parent.

The bodies are the 2026-08-13 text verbatim. What is added is a status banner
and fifteen CORRECTION blocks, each sitting immediately above the section it
affects, so a reader who ignores the ledger still cannot follow a wrong
instruction without seeing the correction first. The full claim-by-claim
verdict, including everything that could NOT be settled from source and needs
a live node, is in BLOCH-G4-DOCS-VERIFICATION-2026-09-01.md.

The three findings that made "correct in place, do not publish" the only
honest option:

  - The transaction document's §10 is now the OPPOSITE of the truth. It
    reports the entire carried opening ledger as unspendable, and calls that
    the single most important thing to know before scheduling an integration.
    `transition.rs:1361-1366` `owns()` implements exactly the 20-byte-prefix
    rule §10.3 predicted; carried outputs open today for the Genesis-3 key.
  - The RPC document teaches, as a worked and recommended example, the exact
    zero-input transfer that halted the chain at slot 69 — and reports that
    stall two sections later as an undiagnosed liveness risk. It was diagnosed
    the same day, by the same author, in 72de2e93. Admission refuses that
    transaction now and returns -32008, a code the document's error table does
    not carry at all.
  - Both printed hex blobs in §2.4 and §3.4 are transcription-truncated (122
    and 123 bytes against a stated 124), and §8 tells an integrator to assert
    them. The quoted signing_root and txid are CORRECT — recomputed here from
    the true preimage and matching to the byte. The corrected blobs were
    regenerated from the field values rather than retyped.

Both documents state correctly that sendrawtransaction's tx_hash is not a
txid, which is one of the four things sibling documents get wrong. Neither
repeats any of the other three.

Description: Detected a Generic API Key, potentially exposing access to various services and sensitive operations.
Author: Tiago Acioli
Message:
explorer: a finality page that shows the guarantee and its support

Genesis-4 has explicit finality and the explorer never showed it. The obvious
rendering is a green tick, and on this chain that is a lie: the quorum
denominator is leak-adjusted with no binding floor, and `finalized` is not a
latch across a reorg.

The page is built on three moves instead:

  - finality as a POSITION, not a state. Epochs sit on three tiers and the
    bracket underneath spans everything unfinalized. A stall is a bar that
    grows sideways across the page; no number has to be read for it to be
    alarming.
  - the support drawn inside the claim, AND the missing measurement drawn as
    missing. The finalized rail is dashed because the quantity that decides
    what belongs on it - two thirds of the leak-adjusted stake - is exposed by
    no RPC, and the page says so where the number would have gone.
  - evidentiary grades on every figure. asserted / modelled / reported /
    constant, in the same glance as the number, because an asterisk defers the
    qualification to a footnote and hopes.

A stall band with sourced thresholds is the loudest object on the page, and
`?replay=stall|rewind|conflict` drives the same components from fixtures so
the stall rendering is exercised before the day it matters.

Reads go through a new /g4 Pages Function that asks BOTH keyless archivals and
reports whether they agreed on the finality claim; the soft public proxy
returns one node's opinion and does not say so. Validators are never polled.
Historical epochs are left to the indexer rather than widening this page's own
polling.

Corrections this change also makes:

  - three figures an earlier draft carried as measured ("27 stalls", "longest
    45 epochs", "one node fakes a quorum at 28 epochs") appear nowhere in the
    repository, and two of the tests it cited do not exist. Replaced with
    sourced thresholds: 4 (constant), 25 (modelled), 56 (asserted), 90-110
    (reported from production).
  - summing attestation_count is NOT participation - duplicates are legal,
    missed proposals delete cast votes, reorgs rescore the past, and consensus
    counts a deduplicated set in stake. Relabelled throughout as inclusion.
  - the non-latch is by inspection of the adopt path, not by test. Our own
    audit says no such test exists; the page says so.
  - the slot page claimed reversing a finalized block would require burning a
    third of the bonded stake. Slashing evidence is encoded one-way and cannot
    reach a verifier (EvidenceNotDecodable), so that penalty is unenforceable.
    Claim removed and recorded as the third defect.

Deploys nothing.
